questions.answer: Yes, 75 days is inside the 90-day backdate limit; period ends 4/2/2027 (13 months inclusive of backdate); $30,000 more; 4.00%; LOI fails at $42,000, escrowed shares (about 5% of stated intent) liquidated to collect the 4% vs 5% difference, no obligation to complete, shares always redeemable.

questions.prompt: Cash-account buy of 500 XYZ regular way Tue 9/15/2026, unpaid. Which statement is correct?
questions.answer: C. T+1 settlement lands Wed 9/16; Reg T adds two business days beyond the settlement cycle, so payment is due Fri 9/18 (T+3). Firm may request an SRO extension; absent one it sells out and the account is frozen 90 calendar days. $1,000-or-less unpaid amounts may be disregarded.

questions.prompt: Which statement about UITs, closed-end and open-end funds is TRUE?
questions.answer: B. CEFs may issue senior securities (bonds at 300% asset coverage, preferred at 200%); open-end funds may issue only one class of voting common stock. UITs are unmanaged with a fixed portfolio and a termination date; premium/discount to NAV applies to CEFs, not open-end shares.

questions.prompt: Why can a limited partner in a real estate DPP not deduct partnership losses against salary, and what can those losses offset?
questions.answer: A DPP is a flow-through entity so losses pass to partners untaxed at the entity level, but a limited partner interest is passive by definition, so the losses offset only passive income, not earned or portfolio income; unused losses carry forward and free up fully on complete disposition of the interest.

questions.prompt: Distinguish full trading authorization from limited trading authorization on a third party account in one sentence, and state what limited authorization does not permit.
questions.answer: Full authorization permits trading plus withdrawal of cash/securities; limited (trading only) authorization permits buying and selling but never withdrawal of cash or securities.

questions.prompt: 45-year-old, first SIMPLE IRA contribution 14 months ago, withdraws $20,000 with no exception applying. Penalty in dollars, and why different from a traditional IRA?
questions.answer: $5,000 (25% penalty, not the usual 10%, applies to SIMPLE IRA distributions within the first 2 years from the date of the first contribution; drops to standard 10% after that window).

questions.prompt: Rep posts a pre-written LinkedIn article (static) vs. replies live to a social media DM (interactive) asking for a stock recommendation. Which is correct under FINRA Rule 2210?
questions.answer: B. Static content (LinkedIn article) is retail communication requiring principal approval before use; interactive content (live DM reply) is correspondence, risk-based supervision rather than pre-use approval. Both must still meet content standards and be retained (generally 3+ years).
